why: A mechanical split, character for character, of one switch into per-route parts files, with a scan test, the pay-routes graph test, bundle budgets and a long e2e list. It touches the cart, checkout and order routes and nine page files at once. RolePage's new storePart prop is optional, so a page that is not given its parts module type-checks and silently draws no working parts: the scan only checks that the cases are in the parts files, not that each page passes them. Only the e2e page-roles spec would notice. Commit 1 (the cookie button split) is small and checked by type check and cookie e2e.
harm_if_wrong: A missed storePart prop or a mis-copied case (a dropped drawTerms or drawGift flag) could leave the checkout without its terms box or payment part, or the cart without its gift option, in production.
make_it_cheaper: Add to store-part-drawers.scan.test.ts a case that each listed page file passes `storePart={<route>Parts}` to every RolePage element, and make the prop required for those routes.
brief_problems: It says the switch has '44 case labels'. src/components/store-part-section.tsx has 42 today (the cases the brief lists also add up to 42), so a cheap executor counting labels will not reach 44.
The paths assume step 2.2's (shop) group. Each file says where it will be, but the executor must still check that 2.2 is in (stop_if covers it).
